claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations using an embedded atom model potential can be used to study the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Nanoparticle size is the variable to be changed when studying the thermal response.
Atomic arrangement and bonding mediate the size-dependent thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
An EAM-based molecular dynamics model can predict melting point as a function of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticle size.
An EAM-based molecular dynamics model can predict thermal conductivity as a function of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticle size.
Bulk FeCuCrCoNi material properties provide a baseline for the nanoparticle calculations.
The proposed nanoparticle-size domain is 1–100 nm.
The accuracy of the EAM potential for FeCuCrCoNi is a source of uncertainty.
Computational resources and simulation time constrain the proposed molecular dynamics study.
The simulation predictions can be tested by comparison with experimental melting-point and thermal-conductivity measurements.
A significant deviation between simulated and experimental thermal responses would falsify the hypothesis.
